PullRequest.Title: sessions: keep disconnected SSH and WSL remotes connectable
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #348758

Disconnecting an SSH or WSL remote deleted its saved entry (SSH) or its cached distribution (WSL), which disposed the remote's sessions provider. Its session disappeared from the Sessions list and an open chat lost its provider, so it had no "Disconnected" banner with a Connect action.

**Changes**

- Disconnecting keeps the entry and remembers the disconnect by address in machine-local application storage (`remoteAgentHost.disconnectedHosts`). Flagged entries are excluded from the dialed entries, so neither reconciliation nor auto-connect dials them.
- The SSH and WSL contributions keep a provider for a flagged remote. It is shown as disconnected and connectable on demand, and its cached sessions are unpublished until it connects again, as with other remote kinds.
- Connecting explicitly clears the flag; that dial counts as user-initiated, including when reconciliation starts it. Removing the remote (new `removeOnDemand`) still forgets it, and clears the flag.
- Keep Sharing as a GitHub environment is unaffected: the disconnected remote is no longer a configured entry, so its environment still takes over its sessions.

**How to test**

1. In the Agents window, connect to an SSH host or a WSL distribution and open one of its sessions.
2. Disconnect it from the Remotes editor (decline keeping it shared, if offered).
3. The open chat shows the remote as disconnected with **Connect**, the remote stays listed in the Remotes editor, and its sessions leave the Sessions list. Reload the window: it stays disconnected and is not dialed.
4. Click **Connect**: the remote connects and its sessions come back.
5. Remove the remote instead: it is forgotten.

**Validation**

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `scripts\test.bat --reporter dot --runGlob "{vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/**/*.test.js,vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/**/*.test.js,vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/*.test.js,vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/*.test.js}"`: passed (3252 passing, 2 pending)
- `node build/hygiene.ts <changed files>`, `node build/lib/formatter.ts --replace --verify <changed files>`, `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed
- `pnpm run check-cyclic-dependencies`: passed
- Not run: manual end-to-end SSH/WSL flow.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The timer, retained cached entries, post-probe filtering, IPC forwarding, and unconditional cp.spawn in runWslCommand are directly traced. Only the duration and user prevalence are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: One shared-process IPC request and one wsl.exe --list --running --quiet subprocess per poll per Agents window.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One grouped probe per five-minute tick per open Agents window, independent of disconnected-distro count; the persisted flag/cache combination keeps this recurring across reloads. It is not a per-distro subprocess fan-out.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary recurring background process creation and IPC work while all WSL remotes are intentionally disconnected.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Disconnect removed the cached distro. With the last cached distro removed, _getProviderEntries() returned an empty list and the poll returned before issuing any IPC request or spawning wsl.exe.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Intentionally disconnected distros remain in the collection that enables the five-minute running-state poll, but are excluded only after the subprocess result has been fetched.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added isDisconnected check at line 99 runs only after the await listRunningDistros() at line 97. The changed _disconnectWSLOnDemand now passes { keepEntry: true }, so _getProviderEntries() continues returning that cached distro and the entries.length === 0 guard no longer skips the probe after the last remote is disconnected.
Findings.Title: Skip the WSL probe when all cached distros are disconnected
Findings.Impact: After disconnecting the only cached WSL remote, leaving the Agents window open still launches wsl.exe every five minutes although no distro is eligible for reconnection. This adds avoidable background process/IPC overhead, including after reload.
Findings.Evidence: WSLAgentHostContribution installs a five-minute timer (lines 34 and 79). _reconnectNewlyRunningDistros obtains all cached distros through _getProviderEntries(), awaits _wslService.listRunningDistros(), then applies the new disconnected check. WSLRemoteAgentHostService.listRunningDistros forwards over IPC to node/wslRemoteAgentHostService.ts:181, which calls runWslCommand(['--list', '--running', '--quiet']); node/wslRemoteAgentHostHelpers.ts:79 unconditionally spawns wsl.exe. There is no result cache or shared in-flight probe.
Findings.Recommendation: Filter intentionally disconnected distros before the empty-entries guard and before listRunningDistros(), retaining one grouped probe only when at least one eligible distro remains.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disconnect or remove an SSH/WSL remote from the Remotes editor or provider actions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The disconnect records suppression synchronously before awaiting shared-process teardown, then removes the renderer connection and reconciles providers. Removal instead deletes saved metadata and clears suppression. Persisting application storage to the database is buffered, not synchronously awaited by these actions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the shared-process disconnect to dispose SSH sessions or WSL relays/bootstrap ownership.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One disconnect request per selected connection key/distro, plus existing relay-release operations associated with disposing that connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shared-process disconnect followed deleting the saved SSH entry or cached WSL distro.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The disconnect action awaits this teardown; retaining the saved entry does not add another remote teardown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Buffer disconnected-address metadata changes and flush grouped application-storage updates through database.updateItems.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical flag-key change when the selected address changes state; multiple writes in the flush interval are grouped. Removal also updates the existing saved-entry key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Disconnect mutated the saved-entry/cache key instead of preserving it and recording a separate disconnected flag. Existing application-storage persistence was already buffered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cache mutation and events are synchronous, while the database flush is deferred.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Normally one selected SSH connection key or WSL distro; a legacy SSH key can resolve to multiple saved entry addresses. Flag serialization scales with the total disconnected-address set, not session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Metadata mutations for matched SSH addresses are synchronous and sequential. One main-service disconnect is issued for the selected key/distro. Connection disposal and provider clearConnection release connection listeners and state subscriptions; provider ownership remains until explicit removal or feature disablement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Disconnected flags and saved entries are read from application storage's in-memory cache. Setting an unchanged flag is a no-op. Removal clears the flag; WSL inventory eviction also clears flags for missing distros. The logical storage mutations are buffered/coalesced for database updates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced both action hooks through storage mutation, main-process disconnect, renderer disposal, and provider connection cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Legacy-key multiplicity and session-cache size vary. No teardown or storage timings were measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression on the action's critical path: teardown cardinality is unchanged, and retaining the provider is the required connectable-offline behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reload the Agents window with intentionally disconnected SSH and WSL remotes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AfterRestored contributions reconstruct provider registrations synchronously. Factories exclude flagged entries before connection reconciliation, so disconnected hosts do not block progress on remote bootstrap or network authentication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse disconnected-address metadata and deserialize persisted session summaries into adapters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Flag-set parsing occurs on observable refreshes and WSL status checks; provider hydration restores at most the existing 100-summary snapshot per retained host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An intentionally disconnected SSH/WSL remote was forgotten, so it had no provider to reconstruct on reload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous renderer work during provider registration after window restoration; no new filesystem/network wait is attached to hydration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H saved disconnected hosts; persisted session summaries are capped at 100 per host by the existing cache writer. Provider and adapter work scales with retained hosts and those summaries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider construction and cache hydration run synchronously in renderer reconciliation. SSH derives connectable/disconnected views from one observable source. WSL entry-change reconciliation is scheduled with RunOnceScheduler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Flags survive reload. Metadata reads use cached application storage; provider construction restores persisted session summaries, then unpublishes them. Repeated unpublish calls return once unpublished, and setConnection ignores an unchanged connection. No disconnected-host listSessions call is issued.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced entry filtering, provider creation, immediate cache hydration, the 100-entry persistence cap, and idempotent unpublishing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of saved hosts and adapter construction costs are unmeasured. Existing open-session state is deliberately retained to preserve reconnectable chats.
Scenarios.Verdict: Additional provider state is intentional and bounded by saved-host ownership; no independent high-confidence actionable memory/startup regression established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicitly reconnect a previously disconnected SSH host or WSL distro.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Stage configuration or mark user restoration, clear suppression, join/start the renderer dial, await transport/bootstrap and protocol initialization, then refresh sessions on the live connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or bootstrap the selected SSH/WSL transport through the main service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective factory attempt per normalized address; competing reconciliation/explicit callers join the pending attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Explicitly reconnecting/adding the remote already used these transport-acquisition boundaries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve an SSH alias with ssh -G, or probe WSL platform and spawn its bootstrap shell when a new main-process session is needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SSH config resolution per new configured-host session; WSL platform/bootstrap operations per new distro session, not per session row. Existing/pending main-process sessions are reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subprocess operations were required for a cold user connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold connection creation waits on these existing operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish SSH/relay transport, perform initialization, and request the host's session list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per effective host connection; listing is aggregated at the host and coalesced by the existing refresh machinery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Connection setup and host-wide session enumeration already crossed these boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Transport and initialization gate connection readiness; session listing updates the provider afterward.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected normalized address; SSH config hosts may share a main-process SSH session by connection key. Session listing is host-wide, not a transport bootstrap per cached session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RemoteAgentHostService joins _pendingConnects by normalized address, so reconciliation and the explicit reconnect do not create duplicate dials. Renderer service pending maps and main-process SSH/WSL session maps also coalesce per key/distro. Independent hosts may connect concurrently as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The staged configuration is published before clearing suppression. SSH user-restored markers are consumed by the factory. Existing shared-process sessions may be reused; cold sessions resolve platform/CLI state and bootstrap. Provider session refreshes coalesce an in-flight listing with at most a trailing listing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced clear/stage ordering and both renderer and main-process coalescing; no increased effective dial cardinality found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold SSH authentication, CLI installation, and WSL startup durations depend on the machine and network; no measurements were taken.
Scenarios.Verdict: No duplicate-dial or new critical-path boundary regression found.

Scenarios.Scenario: Leave an Agents window idle after disconnecting its only cached WSL distro, with the Remotes editor closed.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The five-minute contribution timer runs off the user-interaction critical path. It reads cached provider entries, awaits the running-distro probe, and only afterward excludes intentionally disconnected distros.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the shared process for currently running WSL distributions despite having no eligible reconnect target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request every five minutes per idle Agents window, not per distro.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Disconnecting the last distro removed it from the cache, so the existing entries.length === 0 guard issued zero requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background-only work; no useful reconnect can follow when every cached distro is flagged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn wsl.exe --list --running --quiet and buffer/decode its output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subprocess per grouped probe, every five minutes per window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Zero contribution-owned WSL probe subprocesses after the last cached distro was disconnected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unnecessary background process creation, not foreground latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At least one cached distro, all intentionally disconnected; one grouped probe per timer tick regardless of distro count. Cost grows with idle window lifetime and number of open Agents windows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One uncached IPC/subprocess probe per five-minute tick per window. The helper's 30-second timeout bounds a probe below the normal timer period; there is no cross-window coalescing. No reconnect is issued for flagged distros.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Keeping the cached distro defeats the former empty-list early return. The disconnected flag survives reload. listRunningDistros has neither a result cache nor in-flight sharing on this call path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: complete timer-to-cp.spawn path and before/after cache cardinality are established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Subprocess duration and energy impact are unmeasured. Low frequency and background placement limit severity, not confidence in the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one low-severity eager-work regression; prefilter disconnected distros before deciding whether to probe.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disconnect while keeping the remote shared as a GitHub environment.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing sharing confirmation runs before provider disconnect. Keep Sharing starts inventory refresh without awaiting it; Stop Sharing waits at most the existing five-second timeout. The disconnected direct address leaves configuredEntries, allowing the environment ownership path to continue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the GitHub environment inventory through listEnvironments with refresh enabled after choosing Keep Sharing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical refresh trigger for the selected action, serving the entire environment inventory; not per retained direct-provider session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same confirmation branch already started this inventory refresh when the direct remote entry was removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The Keep Sharing branch does not await this refresh, so it does not extend the disconnect critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected shared remote and one logical inventory refresh per Keep Sharing action; refresh lists environments collectively, not once per cached session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sharing mutations use the existing queue. Keep Sharing refresh is fire-and-forget; environment connection attempts coalesce per environment ID. The direct SSH/WSL dial remains suppressed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Inventory can retain cached host metadata. Keeping a disconnected direct provider does not republish its cached sessions or add it back to the dialed configured entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the unchanged sharing confirmation and refresh boundary and verified disconnected direct entries are excluded from factory entries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Inventory response size and remote service latency are unknown, but their frequency and scheduling are not changed by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new sharing-network fan-out or blocking work established.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 03bf86b8297ca0780c70f56400b80e8cf9381b21. Inspected the complete 16-file inventory and every diff page, including tests and documentation; traced provider ownership, connection coalescing, storage batching, bootstrap boundaries, idle polling, and sharing handoff. Submitted one low-severity finding for recurring WSL probes after all cached distros are intentionally disconnected. No concrete performance-regression fix requiring blame provenance was identified. Static read-only review; no runtime timings.
